questions.answer: The derivative \(f'(x)\) measures the instantaneous rate of change of \(f(x)\) with respect to \(x\). Geometrically, it is the slope of the tangent to the graph at \(x\).

The derivative is
\[f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}.\]
The numerator is the change in output and \(h\) is the change in input.

A constant function has zero rate of change. Therefore
\[f'(x)=0.\]

The slope of \(y=x\) is always \(1\). Using the power rule with \(n=1\),
\[\frac{d}{dx}x=1x^0=1.\]

Use the power rule \(\frac{d}{dx}x^n=nx^{n-1}\):
\[f'(x)=5x^4.\]

Use the constant multiple rule and power rule:
\[\frac{dy}{dx}=3\cdot2x=6x.\]

Differentiate term by term:
\[\frac{d}{dx}(4x^3)=12x^2,\quad \frac{d}{dx}(-2x)=-2,\quad \frac{d}{dx}9=0.\]
So \(f'(x)=12x^2-2\).

questions.prompt: If \(s(t)=5t^2\) is position in metres, find the velocity \(v(t)\).
questions.answer:
Velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time:
\[v(t)=\frac{ds}{dt}=10t.\]
The units are metres per second if \(t\) is in seconds.

First differentiate:
\[f'(x)=3x^2-4.\]
Then substitute \(x=2\):
\[f'(2)=3(2)^2-4=12-4=8.\]

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the tangent to \(y=x^2+3x\) at \(x=-1\).
questions.answer:
The tangent slope is \(dy/dx\) at the point. Differentiate:
\[\frac{dy}{dx}=2x+3.\]
At \(x=-1\), the slope is \(2(-1)+3=1\).

questions.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to \(y=x^2\) at \(x=3\).
questions.answer:
Differentiate: \(y'=2x\), so the slope at \(x=3\) is \(6\). The point is \((3,9)\). Using point-slope form,
\[y-9=6(x-3),\]
so \(y=6x-9\).

Acceleration is the derivative of velocity:
\[a(t)=\frac{dv}{dt}=12-6t.\]
This gives the instantaneous change in velocity at time \(t\).

Horizontal tangents occur where \(f'(x)=0\). Differentiate:
\[f'(x)=3x^2-3.\]
Set equal to zero:
\[3x^2-3=0\Rightarrow x^2=1\Rightarrow x=\pm1.\]

questions.prompt: For \(s(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t\), find when the velocity is zero.
questions.answer:
Velocity is
\[v(t)=s'(t)=3t^2-12t+9=3(t^2-4t+3).\]
Set \(v(t)=0\):
\[t^2-4t+3=(t-1)(t-3)=0.\]
Thus velocity is zero at \(t=1\) and \(t=3\).

questions.prompt: For \(f(x)=ax^3+bx\), find conditions on \(a,b\) so \(f'(1)=5\) and \(f'(2)=14\).
questions.answer:
Differentiate: \(f'(x)=3ax^2+b\). The conditions are
\[3a+b=5,\qquad12a+b=14.\]
Subtract the first from the second: \(9a=9\), so \(a=1\). Then \(3+b=5\), so \(b=2\).

questions.prompt: Find \(c\) if the tangent to \(y=x^2+c\) at \(x=1\) passes through \((0,0)\).
questions.answer:
The derivative is \(y'=2x\), so the slope at \(x=1\) is \(2\). The point on the curve is \((1,1+c)\). Tangent equation:
\[y-(1+c)=2(x-1).\]
At \((0,0)\): \(0-(1+c)=-2\), so \(1+c=2\) and \(c=1\).

questions.prompt: A student says the derivative of \(x^4\) is \(x^3\). Identify the error and correct it.
questions.answer:
The student reduced the exponent but forgot to multiply by the original exponent. The power rule is
\[\frac{d}{dx}x^n=nx^{n-1}.\]
So
\[\frac{d}{dx}x^4=4x^3.\]

questions.prompt: Explain why differentiability at \(x=a\) implies continuity at \(x=a\).
questions.answer:
If \(f'(a)\) exists, then
\[\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\to f'(a).\]
For \(h\ne0\), rearrange: \(f(a+h)-f(a)=h\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\). As \(h\to0\), the first factor \(h\to0\) and the quotient tends to a finite number, so the product tends to \(0\). Hence \(f(a+h)\to f(a)\).

questions.prompt: A position graph has derivative \(0\) at one instant. Does that prove the object is at rest forever? Explain.
questions.answer: No. A derivative of \(0\) at one instant means the instantaneous velocity is zero at that instant only. The derivative may be non-zero at nearby times. For example, \(s(t)=t^2\) has \(s'(0)=0\), but \(s'(t)=2t\) is not zero for \(t\ne0\).
